benchmark_data.source_filter: Apnea-ECG and Sleep-EDF rows where signal_type equals recording modality; reconstruction excluded

timestamp_mapping.statement: Original physiological values and within-recording timing were preserved; recording timestamps were deterministically shifted across successive dates only to construct a longitudinal database workload.

configuration.ingestion_method: same PostgreSQL binary COPY payload; timed COPY FROM plus commit only
configuration.cache_method: warm local measurements; no manual OS cache flushing
configuration.analyze: ANALYZE executed on both tables before correctness and query benchmarks

paper_ready_results.ingestion_observation: Full-data ingestion: TimescaleDB was 40.8% faster by median (12.25s vs 20.68s).
paper_ready_results.simple_range_observation: Five-minute ECG indexed range: TimescaleDB 3.7% slower (62.04 ms vs PostgreSQL 59.84 ms).
paper_ready_results.history_observation: Full two-night patient-history retrieval: TimescaleDB 0.6% faster (1283.22 ms vs PostgreSQL 1291.19 ms).
paper_ready_results.aggregation_observation: Two-night five-minute temporal aggregation: TimescaleDB 16.0% faster (43.09 ms vs PostgreSQL 51.28 ms).
paper_ready_results.storage_observation: Uncompressed storage: TimescaleDB used 0.8% more total space (442.32 MB vs 438.73 MB).
paper_ready_results.compression_observation: Timescale historical columnstore reduced its total footprint by 90.7% (442.32 MB to 41.31 MB; 10.71:1).

Do not describe shifted dates as clinical observations or model-evaluation data.
Keep ingestion secondary and report its variability.
